plants.name: Chrysanthemum × morifolium
plants.description: A bushy perennial with dense, layered flower heads in many forms, from pompons to spiders. It is a staple of autumn gardens and is widely grown commercially for cut flowers.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn (September to November in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Cultivated worldwide, especially East Asia, Europe, and North America; native to China
plants.funFact: Chrysanthemums have been cultivated in China for over 2,500 years, and in Japan the flower is the emblem of the Imperial family and is celebrated at an annual festival.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A tall, graceful tree with fern-like leaves that erupts in clouds of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers. Blooming often occurs before the leaves fully emerge, carpeting streets with fallen blossoms.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring to early summer in the Southern Hemisphere (October to December)
plants.location: Native to South America; widely planted in Australia, South Africa (Pretoria), and Argentina
plants.funFact: In Pretoria, South Africa, known as the Jacaranda City, thousands of jacaranda trees bloom each spring, and local lore says a falling blossom on your head brings good luck.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: An evergreen shrub with glossy dark green leaves and delicate, often fragrant single or semi-double flowers. It blooms earlier than most camellias and is valued for bringing color to late autumn gardens.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to early winter (October to December)
plants.location: Native to Japan; cultivated in the southeastern United States, Europe, and Australia
plants.funFact: Camellia sasanqua is related to Camellia sinensis, the plant used to make tea, and its seeds can be pressed for a culinary and cosmetic oil.

plants.name: Euphorbia pulcherrima
plants.description: A shrub whose showy 'flowers' are actually colored bracts surrounding tiny yellow true flowers. In frost-free climates it grows as a large landscape shrub that begins coloring up as nights lengthen.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to winter (November to February)
plants.location: Native to southern Mexico; grown outdoors in tropical and subtropical regions and as a houseplant worldwide
plants.funFact: Poinsettias are short-day plants that need long uninterrupted nights to develop their bract color, which is why they peak around the holiday season.
